newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: Amplats sees drop in Russia PGM supplies.
newsitem.headline: Amplats sees drop in Russia PGM supplies.

text.p: Anglo American Platinum Corp Ltd (Amplats) said on Tuesday it saw a substantial reduction in Russian supplies of Platinum Group Metals which could drain the platinum market's present liquidity.
Amplats Managing Director Barry Davison told Reuters that the market expected Russia to resume supplies of PGM metals on June 22.
But Davison said in an interview that Amplats -- the world's largest platinum producer -- believed that Russia's 1997 supplies would be substantially reduced due to dwindling stocks.
"We do believe that there will be a significant reduction in the level of sales out of Russia in 1997.
"We have said for some time now that faced with ongoing good, solid demand this reduction in supplies from Russia will drain the liquidity of the platinum market," Davison said.
Davison said Amplats would like to see platinum trading in a range of between $425 to $500.
"Those prices are entirely sustainable...as long as there is not too much volatility," he added.
He said Amplats saw a reduction in platinum usage in future in the automobile catalyst industry which has increasingly being using palladium.
But Davison said recent plans by the U.S. Mint to mint platinum coins would result in a demand increase of around 100,000 ounces of platinum.

He said the general outlook for platinum in the future was good especially in the automobile industry with current studies to develop a proton-exchange membrane fuel cell which would be using platinum.
Davison said he expected platinum demand to grow by two percent a year to the year 2010.
"We believe that annual growth will average about two percent."
